newsitem.title: USA: S&P, Moody's say no plans to downgrade Thailand. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: S&P, Moody's say no plans to downgrade Thailand. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]

text.p: Two major U.S. credit rating agencies, Moody's Investors Service and Standard and Poor's, both said they did not plan to downgrade Thailand's long-term credit rating at this time.
A Moody's analyst said the agency was always watching conditions in every country it rates, but that Thailand's rating had not been placed on review for possible downgrade.
Last month, Moody's cut Thailand's short-term credit rating to Prime 2 from Prime 1.
S&P analyst Cem Karacadag said that credit trends in Thailand have in fact been positive, and not negative.
"S&P said there is a stable outlook and does not think there is a deterioration in credit worthiness," Karacadag said.

The Thai stock market fell Thursday on rumors that the country faced potential downgrade's in Moody's A2 long term sovereign ceiling or S&P's single-A foreign currency rating (corrects ratings from "Moody's AA3 rating or S&P's AA-plus rating").
